channel.title: Foreign Policy Journal – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Foreign Policy Journal – Bias and Credibility (foreignpolicyjournal.com)

item.title: WHO Experimenting on African Children without Informed Consent
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) is sponsoring a malaria vaccine study in African children without obtaining informed consent from parents.

item.title: COVID-19 and Mass-Surveillance: Why South Korea’s approach is also anathema to civil liberties
item.description: Big Brother can do wonders during a pandemic, but the granularity of what it gleans is surpassed by the infringement on privacy that it can make.

item.title: SARS-CoV-2 Response: Where Do We Go from Here? (Introduction)
item.description: In response to the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, governments have implemented authoritarian lockdown measures that could easily be doing more harm than good.

item.title: SARS-CoV-2 Response: Imperial College Model and Lockdown Endgame
item.description: The influential Imperial College model governments have used to justify economic shutdown shows that lockdown only delays and worsens the problem long-term.

item.title: COVID-19: What You Need to Know about Fatality Rates
item.description: Inherently overestimated COVID-19 fatality rates have created mass fear and panic, manufacturing consent for extreme and harmful authoritarian policies.

item.title: Afghan Peace is Now About the Art of the Possible, Not the Perfect
item.description: The current political crisis in Afghanistan is actually an important step towards a realistic peaceful solution: a political “unsettlement”.

item.title: What Has Publicly Blaming Cyber Attacks on Governments Solved?
item.description: Blaming cyber attacks on governments has become routine, but has it resulted in accountability, punishment, or reduction in hostile cyber activities?

item.title: Lebanon’s Dubious Second Wave and the Need to End Lockdown
item.description: Lebanon must end its lockdown or face economic, fiscal, and monetary disasters that pose an even greater threat to the country than COVID-19.

item.title: Why Do Taliban Continue to Kill If They Are Serious about Peace?
item.description: The Taliban must alter their zero-sum mentality and seriously commit to bringing peace to Afghanistan before it is too late.

item.title: OpenAI Secures Department Of Defense Agreement After Anthropic Hit With Restrictions
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman confirmed late Friday, February 27, that his company has finalized an agreement with the Department of Defense, permitting its AI models
